Every public HTTP handler must map success and caught failure paths to 2xx, 4xx, or 5xx responses.

What the Standard says

The Standard defines success, user-error, and system-error response categories and makes controllers responsible for mapping core categorical exceptions to the appropriate HTTP responses. cCoder applies the same boundary rule to middleware because it also handles HTTP requests and responses. Read Codes & Responses.

Why it matters

A complete boundary mapping prevents categorical service exceptions from leaking through the HTTP surface and makes every statically visible outcome explicit to clients.

Bad code example

[HttpGet]
public IActionResult GetStudent(int studentId) =>
    Ok(value: studentService.GetStudent(studentId));

Good code example

[HttpGet]
public IActionResult GetStudent(int studentId)
{
    try
    {
        return Ok(value: studentService.GetStudent(studentId));
    }
    catch (StudentValidationException)
    {
        return BadRequest();
    }
    catch (StudentServiceException)
    {
        return StatusCode(statusCode: 500);
    }
}
